title: Problem 10
markdown:
### Problem
The sum of several positive numbers is 10, and the sum of their squares is greater than 20. Prove that the sum of the cubes of these numbers is greater than 40.

### Solution (adapted from the official solution)
Let $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ be positive real numbers such that

$$\sum_{i=1}^n a_i = 10 \quad \text{and} \quad \sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2 > 20.$$

By the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality applied to vectors $u = (\sqrt{a_1}, \dots, \sqrt{a_n})$ and $v = (a_1^{3/2}, \dots, a_n^{3/2})$:

$$\left( \sum_{i=1}^n a_i \right) \left( \sum_{i=1}^n a_i^3 \right) = \left( \sum_{i=1}^n (\sqrt{a_i})^2 \right) \left( \sum_{i=1}^n (a_i^{3/2})^2 \right) \ge \left( \sum_{i=1}^n \sqrt{a_i} \cdot a_i^{3/2} \right)^2.$$

Notice that $\sqrt{a_i} \cdot a_i^{3/2} = a_i^2$. Therefore,

$$10 \left( \sum_{i=1}^n a_i^3 \right) \ge \left( \sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2 \right)^2.$$

Since $\sum a_i^2 > 20$, squaring both sides gives:

$$\left( \sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2 \right)^2 > 20^2 = 400.$$

Thus

$$10 \left( \sum_{i=1}^n a_i^3 \right) > 400 \implies \sum_{i=1}^n a_i^3 > 40.$$

### Conceptual Explanation
Applying Cauchy-Schwarz to $\sum a_i$ and $\sum a_i^3$ yields $(\sum a_i)(\sum a_i^3) \ge (\sum a_i^2)^2$. With $\sum a_i = 10$ and $\sum a_i^2 > 20$, dividing $400$ by $10$ immediately gives $\sum a_i^3 > 40$.

### Key Technique
Cauchy-Schwarz inequality on power sums $(\sum a_i)(\sum a_i^3) \ge (\sum a_i^2)^2$.
